subject: Transformation for Interval-Censored Disease Incidence Data

messages.author: 91d53d643859f8d6
messages.subject: Transformation for Interval-Censored Disease Incidence Data
parts:
Hi - 

I was wondering if anyone could help me out with the following problem:

I have data from an outbreak of an infectious disease, with, for example, the following number of new cases observed on each successive day of  the outbreak, i.e. Day 1: 1 case, Day 2: 2 cases, Day 3: 3 cases, Day 4: 0 cases. 

The problem is that the model I would like to fit to the data is a continuous time model, but the onset times for these cases are interval-censored and reported as the day in which the case reported symptoms. So, at t=0, we're at the very beginning of the first day, etc.  This means that an individual who reported illness on day 2 could have become ill at any point on day 2, i.e. at t = 1.75, etc. 

This can be dealt with easily by assuming a uniform prior on the onset times for each case and modeling the latent onset time as a real variable on the range from [d-1, d], where d is the day of reporting. The problem with this is that on days where there are multiple case reports (i.e. most of them), we throw out a potentially important piece of information, which is that these latent onset times also follow some unobserved order, i.e. case 1 must have had onset before case 2, even if they were both reported on day 2. 

At present, I am modeling these onset times as a vector of reals on the range from [0,1] and then adding this value to (d-1) to get the unobserved onset time. My question is whether there's a way to leverage the type of approach used to create unbounded ordered and positive ordered vectors in Stan to create ordered vectors on some bounded interval. 

Any suggestions would be greatly appreciated!

thanks,
Jon Zelner

messages.author: 91d53d643859f8d6
messages.subject: Re: Transformation for Interval-Censored Disease Incidence Data
parts:
Nevermind - I just realized that this can be done using an ordered vector in the same way as one might for ordered logistic or probit regression.

best,
Jon
